15.title: Three Parables of the Lost
15.text: When the Pharisees murmured that Christ received sinners and ate with them, he answered with three parables — the lost sheep, the lost coin, the lost son. Each shows that there is joy in heaven over one sinner that repenteth. The shepherd seeks the one until he finds it; the woman lights a candle and sweeps the house; the father, while the son was yet a great way off, ran and fell on his neck and kissed him. The robe, the ring, and the shoes mark restoration to sonship. The elder brother, refusing to come in, pictures those who serve out of duty rather than love and resent grace shown to others. The Father pleads also with him: 'It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad.'
